result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of physical buffers or refuge islands increase pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area for pedestrians crossing the wide street.

result.summary: The image shows a wide multi-lane urban roadway with residential buildings directly abutting the sidewalk. There is a lack of pedestrian crossing infrastructure and no physical buffer between the walkway and vehicle traffic, creating a high-speed environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of protected crossing
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or signals are visible for pedestrians to cross this multi-lane road.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Absence of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the sidewalk are directly adjacent to moving traffic with no physical separation like trees or parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median refuge island to reduce the unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians across the three lanes.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with trees or planters to create a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and parallel on-street parking. While sidewalks are present, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings, traffic calming, and significant greenery, creating a roadway-dominated space.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway design may encourage vehicle speeds that are unsafe for a residential area.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross an expansive roadway without designated protection.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would provide a physical buffer and help naturally slow traffic by narrowing the perceived street width.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with continuous sidewalks and row houses. The environment lacks physical buffers between pedestrians and vehicles, and the presence of trash bags and parked cars creates minor obstructions and visibility concerns.
